title: Wei, gwei and ether: crypto units explained
seoTitle: Wei, Gwei and Ether: Crypto Units Explained | CRYPY
description: How wei, gwei and ether relate, why gas is quoted in gwei, and why token amounts depend on decimals. Quick conversions for ETH, BNB and POL amounts.
summary: The units behind every amount and gas price, with quick conversions.
inShort: Gas prices use gwei because the numbers stay readable.
Tokens have their own decimals: 6 for USDC on Ethereum, 18 for most others.

items: **wei:** the smallest unit. Blockchains store every amount as a whole number of wei.
**gwei:** 1,000,000,000 wei (10⁹). Gas prices are quoted in gwei.

blocks.text: The same units apply to BNB on BNB Chain and POL on Polygon: 1 BNB is 10¹⁸ wei, and gas there is quoted in gwei too.

items: A gas price of 20 gwei × 21,000 gas = 420,000 gwei = 0.00042 ETH

blocks.text: Tokens store amounts in their own smallest unit, and each token says how many **decimals** it uses. Most use 18, like ETH. USDC and USDT on Ethereum use 6, so 1 USDT is stored as 1,000,000. The same token on another chain can use different decimals: USDT on BNB Chain uses 18.
Raw amounts in transaction data are in the smallest unit. Reading them with the wrong decimals makes an amount look a trillion times bigger or smaller than it is.
The [Unit Converter](tool:unit-converter) converts between wei, gwei, ETH and BNB exactly, with no rounding, including amounts in scientific notation. It runs in your browser; nothing is sent.

faq.q: Why not just use ETH for gas prices?
faq.a: Gas prices in ETH would be numbers like 0.000000015. Gwei keeps them readable: 15 gwei.

faq.q: Where does the name wei come from?
faq.a: It honours Wei Dai, a cryptography pioneer. Gwei means giga-wei: a billion wei.
No. Most do, but stablecoins often use 6 on Ethereum. Always check the token's decimals before reading raw amounts.
